rows.description: Groups and gossip pull you in. Wise: stay friendly to all, do good work, and avoid taking sides. Immature: passing tales for safety.

rows.description: New in the team you are left out of lunches and chats. Wise: introduce yourself, join small conversations, and give it a few weeks. Immature: assuming hostility.

rows.description: You are given menial work with no learning. Wise: ask for a clear role, request feedback, and decide when to move on. Harmful: silently accepting.

rows.description: You are now the one showing an intern the work. Wise: teach patiently and credit their contribution. Immature: dumping your tasks on them.

rows.description: A colleague or superior makes comments or advances that you dislike. Wise: say no clearly, document dates and words, and use the POSH committee or HR. It is not your fault.

rows.description: Your idea or work is presented as theirs. Wise: raise it calmly with evidence, share updates in writing in future, and clarify roles early. Immature: public blowups or sulking.

rows.description: You are tempted to present shared work as yours. Wise: name who did what; trust built is worth more. Harmful: taking credit and rationalising it.

rows.description: A colleague blames you for their mistake. Wise: stay calm, present facts, and involve the manager if needed. Immature: retaliating.

rows.description: Others do little and you carry the load. Wise: set roles early, check in, and raise it politely before deadline. Immature: doing everything silently and resenting.
